```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Dickinson_2014_nevirapine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Dickinson_2014_nevirapine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.02069-13> (open access, PMC3910846)

No erratum or correction to the article was found in Europe PMC (searched
2026-11-20).

# Population

Dickinson 2014 analysed a pharmacokinetic substudy of a prospective cohort of
1,117 antiretroviral-naive HIV-infected adults starting nevirapine-based
therapy at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital, Blantyre, Malawi (2007-2008). The
model was built on 180 patients (101 female, 56%) with 383 serum nevirapine
concentrations. Median (range) age was 34 years (21-62), weight 54 kg (35-94),
BMI 20 kg/m^2 (15-38), CD4 count 156 cells/mm^3 (1-812) and duration of
therapy at sampling 6 weeks (1-26). Twenty-five patients developed nevirapine
hypersensitivity (18 rash, 3 jaundice, 4 Stevens-Johnson syndrome) and 23 were
coinfected with hepatitis B and/or C. All received 200 mg nevirapine twice
daily in a fixed-dose combination with lamivudine and stavudine, except 3
patients still in the 200 mg once-daily lead-in. Forty tolerant patients had
rich sampling (0, 1, 2, 5 and 9 h post-dose); the others contributed one
random sample, with a second one if hypersensitivity developed later.

CYP2B6 c.983T>C was heterozygous (TC) in 17.2% with no CC homozygotes; c.516G>T
was GT in 48.7% and TT in 16.2%. In the final-model genotype groups the
cohort split into 983TT/516GG or GT (n = 102), 983TT/516TT (n = 25),
983TC/516GG or GT (n = 27) and genotype missing (n = 26) (Figure 2 legend).

The same information is available programmatically:
`readModelDb("Dickinson_2014_nevirapine")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(3.02) | Table 1 final model CL/F = 3.02 L/h (RSE 4.44%); reference genotype 983TT with 516GG or GT (Table 1 footnote) |
| `lvc` | log(114) | Table 1 final model V/F = 114 L (RSE 22.8%) |
| `lka` | log(0.578) | Table 1 final model ka = 0.578 1/h (RSE 26.1%) |
| `e_983tt_516tt_cl` | -0.696 | Table 1 final model theta1, CYP2B6 983TT/516TT (RSE 36.6%); Results 'Multiple SNP analysis': -23.0% |
| `e_983tc_cl` | -1.08 | Table 1 final model theta2, CYP2B6 983TC/516GG or GT (RSE 22.3%); Results 'Multiple SNP analysis': -35.8% |
| `etalcl` | log(1 + 0.332^2) = 0.1047 | Table 1 final model IIV CL/F 33.2% (RSE 27.4%) |
| `etaiov_lcl_1..3` | log(1 + 0.318^2) = 0.0963 | Table 1 final model IOV CL/F 31.8% (RSE 24.2%) |
| `propSd` | 0.131 | Table 1 final model proportional residual error 13.1% (RSE 17.0%) |
| `tvcl <- exp(lcl) + e_983tt_516tt_cl * hom_516 + e_983tc_cl * het_983` | n/a | Results 'Pharmacogenetic analysis': CL = CL0 + theta1 GEN1 + theta2 GEN2 (+ theta3 MISS) |
| `cl <- tvcl * exp(etalcl + iov_cl)` | n/a | Results 'Pharmacokinetic and covariate model': CL/F_ij = theta1 x exp(eta_i + kappa_ij) |
| `d/dt(depot)`, `d/dt(central)` | n/a | Results: one-compartment model with first-order absorption |
| `Cc ~ prop(propSd)` | n/a | Results: Y = F x (1 + epsilon1) |

# Typical-value checks

The genotype shifts enter additively on the linear clearance scale, so the
typical CL/F of each group and its percent change from the reference follow
directly. Results 'Multiple SNP analysis' quotes the reductions as 23.0% and
35.8%.

```{r typical-cl}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Dickinson_2014_nevirapine"))
ini_est <- setNames(mod$iniDf$est, mod$iniDf$name)

typ_cl <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("983TT/516GG or GT (reference)", "983TT/516TT", "983TC/516GG or GT"),
  cl = exp(ini_est[["lcl"]]) +
    c(0, ini_est[["e_983tt_516tt_cl"]], ini_est[["e_983tc_cl"]])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_change = 100 * (cl / cl[1] - 1),
    published_pct = c(0, -23.0, -35.8),
    half_life_h = log(2) * exp(ini_est[["lvc"]]) / cl,
    auc_tau_ss = 200 / cl
  )

stopifnot(all(abs(typ_cl$pct_change - typ_cl$published_pct) < 0.1))

typ_cl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype group" = group,
    "Typical CL/F (L/h)" = cl,
    "Change (%)" = pct_change,
    "Published change (%)" = published_pct,
    "t1/2 (h)" = half_life_h,
    "AUCtau,ss 200 mg (mg*h/L)" = auc_tau_ss
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical CL/F by CYP2B6 genotype group.")
```

# Virtual cohort

The cohort reproduces the genotype mix of the Dickinson 2014 analysis data set
(Figure 2 legend): 102 reference, 25 983TT/516TT and 27 983TC/516GG or GT
subjects. The 26 subjects with missing genotype are simulated as reference
genotype because the missing-genotype shift (theta3) is not reported. Each
subject takes 200 mg twice daily for 14 days, which is more than 10 half-lives
of the typical 26-h half-life, and is then followed for 30 h after the last
dose with no further dosing, as in the Figure 2 simulation. One sampling
occasion is simulated (`OCC = 1`), so each subject carries one draw of the
inter-occasion effect.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20141001)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20141001)

geno_groups <- tibble::tibble(
  group = c("983TT/516GG or GT", "983TT/516TT", "983TC/516GG or GT", "missing (as reference)"),
  n = c(102L, 25L, 27L, 26L),
  SNP_CYP2B6_RS28399499_C_COUNT = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 0L),
  SNP_CYP2B6_RS3745274_T_COUNT = c(1L, 2L, 0L, 1L)
)

subjects <- geno_groups |>
  tidyr::uncount(n) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

tau <- 12
n_doses <- 28L
t_last <- (n_doses - 1L) * tau

doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, dose_n = seq_len(n_doses)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = (dose_n - 1) * tau, amt = 200, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")

obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = subjects$id, tad = seq(0, 30, by = 0.5)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = t_last + tad, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::left_join(subjects, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(OCC = 1L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("group")
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
  dplyr::filter(tad >= 0)
```

# Replicate Figure 2: 90% prediction interval after the last dose

Figure 2 of Dickinson 2014 shows the median and 5th/95th percentiles of 1,000
simulated patients against time after dose. Read from the figure, the median
is about 5.5 mg/L at the pre-dose time, peaks near 6.3 mg/L at about 5 h and
falls to about 3.5 mg/L at 30 h; the 5th and 95th percentiles start near 2.2
and 13-14 mg/L.

```{r figure-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
pi_all <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    P05 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    P50 = stats::median(Cc),
    P95 = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(pi_all, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = P05, ymax = P95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = P50), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = P05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = P95), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, colour = "red", linetype = "dotdash") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Nevirapine (mg/L)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 2 of Dickinson 2014",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of 180 simulated patients at steady state on 200 mg twice daily; red line: 3 mg/L MEC."
  )

pi_all |>
  dplyr::filter(tad %in% c(0, 5, 12, 30)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-tad, \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time after dose (h)" = tad) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated percentiles (mg/L) at selected times.")
```

The same summary by genotype group shows both variant groups above the
reference. The typical-value table orders them (983TC/516GG or GT has the
lowest CL/F); with only 25-27 simulated subjects in each variant group the
group medians carry about 10% Monte Carlo error, enough to swap the two
variant groups in a given draw.

```{r figure-2-by-group, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(group, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(P50 = stats::median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, P50, colour = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, colour = "red", linetype = "dotdash") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)",
    y = "Median nevirapine (mg/L)",
    colour = "CYP2B6 group",
    title = "Median simulated profile by genotype group"
  )
```

# Steady-state trough concentrations

Dickinson 2014 predicted the 12-h trough for every patient-occasion (n = 219):
median 5.25 mg/L (range 0.55-23.39), with 22 of 219 (10%) below the 3.0 mg/L
minimum effective concentration. All troughs below 3 mg/L were in the
983TT/516GG or GT and 983TT/516TT groups; none were in the 983TC group.

```{r trough}
trough <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(tad == tau)

trough_summary <- trough |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_ctrough = stats::median(Cc),
    pct_below_mec = 100 * mean(Cc < 3)
  )

trough_by_group <- trough |>
  dplyr::group_by(group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    median_ctrough = round(stats::median(Cc), 2),
    pct_below_mec = round(100 * mean(Cc < 3), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Structural check on the centre of the distribution: a mis-transcribed
# clearance or volume moves the median trough by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(trough_summary$median_ctrough / 5.25 - 1) < 0.2)

trough_by_group |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype group" = group,
    "N" = n,
    "Median Ctrough (mg/L)" = median_ctrough,
    "% < 3 mg/L" = pct_below_mec
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated steady-state trough (12 h post-dose) by genotype group.")
```

Overall, the simulated median trough is
`r round(trough_summary$median_ctrough, 2)` mg/L (published 5.25 mg/L) and
`r round(trough_summary$pct_below_mec, 1)`% of simulated troughs fall below
3 mg/L (published 10%). The published values are empirical Bayes predictions,
which shrink towards the typical value, so the simulated proportion below the
MEC, which carries the full inter-individual and inter-occasion variance, is
expected to be somewhat higher.

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the steady-state dosing interval (0-12 h after
the last dose) by genotype group.

```{r pknca}
conc_ss <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), tad <= tau) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, time = tad, Cc, treatment = group)

dose_ss <- conc_ss |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 200)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ss, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "extravascular")

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0,
  end = tau,
  cmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cav = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = stats::median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype group" = treatment,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin,
    "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast,
    "Cav (mg/L)" = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated steady-state NCA parameters by genotype group.")
```

The median AUC0-12 of each group estimates the typical-value `200 / CL/F`
of the typical-value table above (66.2, 86.1 and 103.1 mg*h/L), since the
median of a log-normally varying AUC equals the typical-value AUC; the two
variant groups (25-27 subjects each) carry about 10% Monte Carlo error.

## Comparison against published exposure

The Discussion reports median individual predictions of Cmax and Ctrough for
patients without hypersensitivity of 6.1 and 5.2 mg/L. These are empirical
Bayes predictions in the full analysis cohort; the comparison below pools the
simulated cohort with the same genotype mix.

```{r nca-compare}
reference <- data.frame(cmax = 6.1, cmin = 5.2)

nca_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
    dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin")),
  reference,
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L")
)
knitr::kable(nca_cmp, caption = "Simulated versus published median steady-state exposure (Dickinson 2014 Discussion).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Missing-genotype shift not reported.** The covariate equation includes a
  separate shift theta3 for patients with missing genotype data, but Table 1
  does not report its value. The packaged model has no missing-genotype term;
  a subject with unknown genotype must be assigned a genotype (the vignette
  simulates the 26 missing-genotype subjects as reference).
- **Genotype combinations outside the data.** No 983CC homozygotes were
  observed, so a C-allele count of 2 receives no 983 shift. The combination
  983TC/516TT is not described; the model adds both shifts for it (1.24 L/h).
  The Results paragraph on concentrations below the MEC lists a "983TC/516TT"
  group, but the following sentence says none of those concentrations came
  from 983TC patients, so this is read as 983TT/516TT.
- **IIV and IOV as coefficients of variation.** Table 1 reports IIV and IOV on
  CL/F as percentages of exponential (log-normal) random effects. They are
  converted with omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2), as in the related
  `Schipani_2011_nevirapine` model from the same group; reading them as
  sqrt(omega^2) instead would raise each variance by about 5%. The residual
  error is the proportional SD (0.131).
- **Number of occasions.** The paper does not state how many occasions a
  patient could contribute. Three occasion slots are provided (an intensive
  sampling day plus up to two random samples), each with the single estimated
  IOV variance. rxode2 has no occasion level for random effects, so the
  occasion effect is a sum of per-occasion etas selected by `OCC`
  indicators. rxode2 therefore cannot mu-reference those etas and warns
  "some etas defaulted to non-mu referenced" on each solve; simulation is
  unaffected, and the only cost would be slower estimation if the model were
  refitted.
- **Steady state and autoinduction.** The model describes concentrations
  during maintenance dosing; autoinduction during the lead-in was not
  modelled (adding week 1-3 samples did not improve the fit). The 3 patients
  sampled during the once-daily lead-in are not represented separately.
- **Figure 3 not reproduced.** Figure 3 simulates Yoruba and Caucasian
  populations with separate single-SNP models (983T>C alone and 516G>T alone)
  whose parameters are reported only in part, and with HapMap allele
  frequencies that are not printed in the paper. Only the final combined
  model is packaged.
- **Cohort size.** Figure 2 used 1,000 simulated patients; the vignette uses
  the 180-patient genotype mix of the analysis data set.
